anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

choices.why: Stoic-tinged: coming to a firm hold of the distinction.

pass_a_gloss: How then shall we come onto a road of setting out and come into a grasp whether beginning and the first were said correspondingly or were used as upon other and other, unless we are guided from the like things lying in the writings?
pass_b_english: How then shall we come onto a path to set out, and come to a grasp of whether "beginning" and "first" were said in the same sense, or were used as of one thing and another — unless we are guided [from] the like things that lie in the Scriptures?
source_text: Πῶς οὖν εἰς ὁδὸν ἔλθωμεν τοῦ|| ἐπιβῆναι καὶ εἰς κατάληψιν ἐλθεῖν πότερον καταλλήλως ἡ ἀρχὴ καὶ τὸ πρῶτον ἐρρέθη ἢ ὡς ἐφ’ [ἑ]τέρου καὶ <ἑτέρου> ἐχρήσθη, εἰ μὴ [ἀπὸ] τῶν ὁμοίων ἐν ταῖς γρ[αφαῖ]ς κειμένων ὁδηγηθ[εῖμ]εν.
